subject: Request: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support
messages:
From: Rebecca Hayes <rebecca.hayes@brightbridge.health>
To: logan_wright@gmail.com
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We appreciate the roadmap call and the clear plan to add native embedding support for the new multimodal flows — BrightBridge has been planning a Q3 pilot that depends on that feature.

Unfortunately, the updated ETA you shared during the product sync (end of July) pushes our pilot by at least six weeks due to integration gating and privacy review. That delay is material for our go-live commitments to two hospital systems.

Can Redwood provide a one-time commercial adjustment (credit or rebate) to offset the delay while we wait for embedding support? We're not asking for a long-term discount — more of a compensatory credit tied to the specific missed milestone. I attached a short impact summary and a proposed adjustment outline.

Happy to jump on a call this week — Rebecca.

--
Rebecca Hayes
Head of Partnerships, BrightBridge Health
rebecca.hayes@brightbridge.health
(415) 555-4812

From: logan_wright@gmail.com
To: Rebecca Hayes <rebecca.hayes@brightbridge.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@gmail.com, marcus_lin@gmail.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Rebecca —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. I'm looping in Laura (account lead) and Marcus (commercial ops) so we can evaluate the ask quickly.

Short answer: we hear you and want to be pragmatic. Marcus — can you take a first pass on the commercial adjustment (amount and mechanics) and flag anything that needs leadership sign-off? Laura — I'll coordinate the customer comms once we have an approach.

I'll follow up with a proposed internal cadence today.

Thanks,
Logan

--
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@gmail.com
To: logan_wright@gmail.com, laura_bennett@gmail.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Team —

Reviewed Rebecca's impact summary. Quick notes:
- BrightBridge is ~2.1M ARR and currently on Standard plan with 3-month committed usage.
- Their pilot delay maps to an estimated $45k in incremental infra/engineering cost for them (per their doc).
- Typical one-off adjustments for similar scope recently ranged 3–8% of ARR as credits; lower bound was used for tactical fixes.

Proposal (first pass): 4% one-time invoice credit applied to the next 3 invoices (applied pro rata), plus a technical priority ticket to our product team for early access when feasible. Estimated cost to Redwood: ~US$84k realized as revenue credit.

I think this needs executive approval given the size and the policy precedent. If Leadership signs off on the principle, we can formalize language and the contract amendment.

Marcus

From: laura_bennett@gmail.com
To: logan_wright@gmail.com, marcus_lin@gmail.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@gmail.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Adding Stephanie from Product Operations for technical prioritization commentary.

Logan / Marcus — from the customer relationship standpoint I'd prefer a smaller public-facing credit (2%) paired with a concrete delivery commitment and a short-term SLO addendum. BrightBridge values predictability; a big credit without firm deliverables could set an undesirable expectation.

Stephanie — can product confirm whether we can offer a scoped priority access (beta key + weekly check-ins) that materially shortens BrightBridge's timeline? If so, that strengthens our position to do a modest one-time credit (2%).

Laura

From: stephanie_nguyen@gmail.com
To: laura_bennett@gmail.com, logan_wright@gmail.com, marcus_lin@gmail.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Hi all —

Product operations update: we can offer BrightBridge a scoped early-access build (+ feature flag) and a named support lane for 8 weeks. That would require a small engineering allocation (approx. 1.0 FTE equivalent over 6 weeks) and a commitment from BrightBridge to share integration telemetry.

If we pair the early access with weekly syncs and a short SLO addendum, I support keeping the commercial credit modest (2%). Without early access the credit needs to be larger per precedent.

Happy to draft the technical terms for legal review.

—Stephanie
Product Ops

From: logan_wright@gmail.com
To: Rebecca Hayes <rebecca.hayes@brightbridge.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@gmail.com, marcus_lin@gmail.com, stephanie_nguyen@gmail.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact + ask: compensatory adjustment for deferred embedding support

Rebecca —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Short summary of the outcome:

1) Redwood will provide a one-time account credit equal to 2% of BrightBridge's ARR, applied across the next three invoices.
2) We will enable an early-access build (feature-flagged) with a named support lane and weekly integration syncs for up to 8 weeks.
3) The credit and early-access terms will be captured in a short amendment; Marcus will draft the commercial language and Stephanie will draft the technical scope.

If BrightBridge is comfortable with that approach, I'll route the amendment for signatures and prioritize the kickoff call next week.

Appreciate you raising this — looking forward to getting the pilot back on track.

Best,
Logan

--
